extracted.intended_audience: military judge advocates, government contracting officers, and other military/legal officers advising on courts of inquiry, articles of war, and bonds
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards governing (1) courts of inquiry and their procedures, opinions, and evidentiary effect under the Articles of War, and (2) the law and practice relating to bonds, bidders' guaranties, and sureties for the War Department and related government contracting contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to copy of court-martial record (Art. 114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person tried by a general court-martial or by a military commission is entitled to one copy of the record of proceedings in his case upon demand therefor made by him or by any person in his behalf before his decease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application should be addressed first to the Judge Advocate General; if not made by the accused himself, applicant must exhibit satisfactory evidence that the applicant represents the accused. A person other than the accused applying on his own account is not entitled to a copy. A copy otherwise than as above can be secured only by order of the Secretary of War. The report of the Judge Advocate General will not be furnished under the one hundred and fourteenth article of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to order a court of inquiry (Art. 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the President nor a commanding officer is obliged to order a court of inquiry on the application of an officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an officer requests a court of inquiry and it is apparent the real purpose is to secure an opinion by the court on a question of patent infringement, it is not a proper subject for a court of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of court of inquiry's examination (Art. 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: The court of inquiry authorized by the one hundred and fifteenth article of war can examine into the nature of transactions of officers or enlisted men only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accused appears and examines witnesses before such a court as freely as before a court-martial. Proceedings of a court of inquiry may be open at the discretion of the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper content and scope of court of inquiry opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inquiry is instituted to assist determination whether the party should be brought to trial, the opinion should state whether further proceedings before a court-martial are called for and give reasons for the conclusions reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the court is convened to investigate a question of military right, responsibility, conduct, etc., its opinion should properly confine itself to the special question proposed and its legitimate military relations. Courts of inquiry, being composed of military men, will rarely be called upon to express opinions upon pure legal questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrence and dissent in courts of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of a court of inquiry directed to express an opinion are not required by law or regulation to concur in their conclusions; the majority does not govern like in a court-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more members cannot conscientiously agree with the majority, they should formally disagree and present separate reports. Such disagreement is material and useful to the reviewing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of court of inquiry proceedings in court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings of a court of inquiry cannot be admitted as evidence on the merits at a trial before a court-martial of an offense for which dismissal will be mandatory upon conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, such proceedings, properly authenticated, would be admissible to impeach a witness on the trial by showing prior inconsistent statements made before the court of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command authority of Marine Corps officers on Army transports
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers of the Marine Corps traveling without troops on Army transports cannot exercise command of the troops on board or exercise command in the Army unless duly assigned thereto by the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities confirm this rule; assignment by the President is required for command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command at joint encampments
rubrics_metrics.description: At joint encampments of the Regular Army and Organized Militia, command remains with the regular post commander without regard to rank of senior officer of the Organized Militia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves regular Army command despite militia seniority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion and accounting for effects of deceased soldier (Arts. 126–127)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under articles 126 and 127 a company commander, within his discretion, may convert into cash the effects left by a deceased soldier, account for them, and pay over proceeds to the personal representatives after defraying expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenses incurred must be defrayed out of the sum realized; after deduction the remainder is the 'net proceeds' referred to in Army Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation for securing effects of deceased (Arts. 126–127)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions for securing effects, making inventory, and accounting to legal representatives apply special reference to deaths while in active service in the field or at remote military posts and then only to effects left 'in camp or quarters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attempt by the commander to secure effects left elsewhere would not be within the authority and might subject the officer to liability as an administrator; upon proper accounting to the duly qualified legal representative the officer's responsibility is discharged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'legal representatives' under Art. 127
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'legal representatives' is to be construed as equivalent to a duly appointed legal personal representative, i.e., the duly appointed executor or administrator of the estate of the deceased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal appointment/qualification is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor disqualification from deliberating on his invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor cannot serve on a board which is considering his invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Board of Officers: 'Inventor can not serve on, which is considering his invention.' This is a conflict-of-interest standard applicable to boards reviewing inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond may be required in absence of statute
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond may be required by the Government even where there is no express statutory authority mandating it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary bonds taken under departmental authority to secure fidelity or performance are valid so long as not in violation of statute or regulations; examples include bonds for disbursing officers, indemnity, or safe-keeping where title is doubtful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder's guaranty purpose and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a bidder's guaranty is to furnish sufficient security that the bidder will enter into contract if his bid is accepted; it should be as formal and legally sufficient as a contractor's bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guaranty is intended to allow the Government to recover the difference if the bidder refuses to enter into contract; it should be prepared to serve as basis for a legal claim by suit if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfatal defects in bidders' guaranties may be waived
rubrics_metrics.description: Defects in bidders' guaranty bonds that are not fatal to validity are in practice waived by the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative waiver is common; specific omissions may be cured by related documents (e.g., accompanying proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantor/partner objections may be waived
rubrics_metrics.description: Objection that a partner was guarantor for a copartner may be waived since it does not affect the validity of the guaranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver does not affect enforceability in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of blanks/omissions in guaranty
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain blank spaces left in a guaranty may not affect validity and may be cured by subsequent facts (e.g., appearance of bidder's name in proposal or time in advertisement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fact patterns determine whether omissions are cured; department practice may treat such defects as waivable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal and formality of bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: A guaranty without a seal may still be effective; bonds not under seal may still be valid contracts; a printed scroll or other device can be a valid substitute for an adhesive seal in most States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance over formality—defects in the form of the seal are often not fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate bonds: name and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate name must be exactly expressed on a bond; the officer signing and attaching the seal should have proper authority to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where authority does not clearly appear and it is impracticable to reexecute, practice may permit acceptance; a copy of records showing selection/qualification of officers should be attached—certificate alone not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds for organizations without legal entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds for organizations having no legal entity should be signed by a proper person as principal; when an individual conducts business under a company name papers should be in the name of the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special practice where institutions (e.g., Soldiers' Home) give bond; in insular administration bonds may need to run in name of United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and witnesses in bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: A contracting officer in a bond may be designated by title alone, and the validity of a bond is not affected by the absence of a witness to the signature of the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical sufficiency of description and execution is recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of bond nonfatal omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Omission of the date of a bond does not affect its validity; differences between the bond date and the date of the resolution authorizing execution are addressed by practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context matters where the bond recites relation to contract dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sureties: binding and consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond should not be accepted unless sureties are clearly bound; erasures and interlineations require consent of sureties; sureties are not bound by supplemental contracts or unauthorized modifications without their assent and not bound beyond the period fixed unless they assent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to secure consent of one surety to a modification may release all sureties. Affidavit of justification may be required; death of one surety on joint and several bond does not raise automatic requirement for new bond in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double aspect of bond (performance and laborers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a bond secures both performance of the contract and payment of laborers/material-men, its obligation as to laborers and material-men is not affected by modification of the contract without surety's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond should clearly state obligations distinguishing aspects (performance vs. payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government practice on bonds after performance
rubrics_metrics.description: It is contrary to the practice of the War Department to surrender bonds after performance or to release sureties simply because work is done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration prefers to retain bonds as security for potential claims; Treasury may have review/control over War Department bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursing officers' bonds—sufficiency and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds of disbursing officers may be required even when no statute prescribes them; such bonds may continue in force notwithstanding the officer not at the moment disbursing funds, and 'office' in the bond refers to the office named and not to another to which promoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sureties generally expected to justify in double the amount; provisions exist regarding substitution of surety companies and filing under military governments or academies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractors' bonds—waiver and assignment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond required of a contractor may be waived where not required by statute; approval of the contract includes acceptance of the bond; the bond cannot be assigned to creditors of the contractor to enable them to sue on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where contract partly performed, new bond may be proportionately reduced; requirements as to amount fixed by regulation may be waived in practice in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational institutions' bonds: authority and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds given by colleges/institutions require evidence that the officer signing has authority (usually shown by records), clear and specific resolutions authorizing execution, and the corporate name and seal properly used; bonds should be accompanied by copy of charter where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General authority may suffice in some cases; bonds must not exceed amounts authorized by the board; certain substantive conditions (e.g., that college can educate 150 male students) must be stated where statutory prerequisites exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate surety—acceptance and evidence of qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate surety may be accepted even without express statutory authorization; however, a copy of the record showing selection and qualification of corporate officers must be attached—certificate of secretary not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surety is bound notwithstanding principal's failure to pay premium in many circumstances; foreign corporations may not be required to comply with State laws prior to doing business with the United States in some contexts. Statutory limits (e.g., bond not greater than ten percent of company's paid-up capital and surplus) and Treasury solvency inquiries apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bonds to indemnify Government agents using non-owned patented articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Where officers representing the United States used patented articles not owned by the contractor from whom obtained, it is recommended that a bond be required from the contractor, before payment, conditioned to indemnify the officers and agents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a precaution because officers/agents may be personally subject to suit even if the United States is immune.
